findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:397-412 (OAuthLoginView.dispatch): The pipeline state is mutated (pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", ...)) before the state parameter is validated. Since the state issued to GitHub is pipeline.signature (a digest of that very pipeline state), any callback whose installation_id was not already bound when the state was issued changes the signature and fails the comparison. GitHub appends installation_id (with setup_action=install) to the OAuth callback on the standard first-time install path, so legitimate installs will be rejected with "We could not verify the authenticity of the installation request." Validate state first, then bind.

[High/security] src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494-496 (GitHubInstallation.dispatch): The installer-verification control is skipped entirely on the Integration.DoesNotExist branch — it binds installation_id and advances without ever consulting github_authenticated_user. For a newly created installation whose webhook has not been processed yet (or failed delivery), there is no sender metadata and no check, so an attacker who enumerates the sequential GitHub installation_id can link a victim's fresh installation to the attacker's Sentry org — exactly the attack this PR is meant to prevent. The check only protects re-linking of already-existing integrations.

[High/test_gap] tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:385-455 (test_github_user_mismatch): This test never reaches the sender-mismatch branch it was written to exercise. Because installation_id is bound before the authorize redirect (changing pipeline.signature), the hardcoded state=9cae… cannot match the callback pipeline's signature, so the test fails at state validation and renders the generic error. The PR's central security comparison (github_authenticated_user vs integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]) is therefore never executed by any test.

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:332-345 and :698-712: test_github_installed_on_another_org and test_github_prevent_install_until_pending_deletion_is_complete send the stale hardcoded state 9cae… after an init request that bound installation_id (which changes the signature). State validation fails and the response is "Invalid installation request.", so the asserted specific errors ("Github installed on another Sentry organization." / pending deletion) cannot be produced — these tests are broken as written. Capture the state from the authorize redirect's Location instead of hardcoding it.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:512-515 (GitHubInstallation.dispatch): integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises an unhandled KeyError (→ 500) for integrations whose metadata lacks "sender" — e.g., integrations created via the pipeline when the installation webhook was missed/late, or rows created before this change. Use .get("sender", {}).get("login") and fail closed on a missing value.

[Medium/security] src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402-412 (OAuthLoginView.dispatch): The OAuth state is pipeline.signature, a deterministic digest of pipeline-state contents (org id, installation_id — all low-entropy and guessable/enumerable) rather than a cryptographically random per-flow nonce. If the digest is unkeyed, an attacker can compute a valid state and forge callbacks into a victim's in-flight pipeline, gutting the CSRF binding this check is supposed to provide. Generate and bind_state a random token as the state.

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:385-395 (test_installation_not_found): The test no longer exercises the installation-not-found path — the assertion was changed from "The GitHub installation could not be found." to "Invalid installation request." because the flow now terminates at the OAuth step (state/token exchange) before the 404 installation lookup ever runs. The 404 mock is dead weight, get_installation_info failure handling is now uncovered, and the test name is misleading.

[Low/bug] src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:407-409 (OAuthLoginView.dispatch): redirect_uri (and the other params) are interpolated into the authorize URL via f-string without urlencode. Any reserved query character (&, =, space) in the absolute URI corrupts the query string / breaks the redirect. Build the query with urlencode.

[Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:113-115 and the error() default: The "We could not verify the authenticity of the installation request" message is also returned for transient failures (token exchange failure, user-info fetch failure, inactive integration), misattributing GitHub availability/config problems to authenticity and telling users to restart when restarting won't help. Distinguish these failure modes in the error message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:397-412 (OAuthLoginView.dispatch): The pipeline state is mutated (pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", ...)) before the state parameter is validated. Since the state issued to GitHub is pipeline.signature (a digest of that very pipeline state), any callback whose installation_id was not already bound when the state was issued changes the signature and fails the comparison. GitHub appends installation_id (with setup_action=install) to the OAuth callback on the standard first-time install path, so legitimate installs will be rejected with "We could not verify the authenticity of the installation request." Validate state first, then bind.

adjudication.rationale: While OAuthLoginView.dispatch does call pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", ...) before checking request.GET["state"], the finding’s core claim—that pipeline.signature is a digest of the current pipeline state and therefore changes when bind_state is called—is not shown anywhere in this diff. Additionally, in the shown flow when no state is present (the redirect-to-GitHub step), the code binds installation_id (if provided) *before* generating state=pipeline.signature, so the issued state would already reflect that bound value; the added tests exercise this exact path and succeed without any installation_id in the callback. The alleged “legitimate installs will be rejected” behavior depends on external assumptions (GitHub always appending installation_id on callback and signature being state-dependent) that are not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494-496 (GitHubInstallation.dispatch): The installer-verification control is skipped entirely on the Integration.DoesNotExist branch — it binds installation_id and advances without ever consulting github_authenticated_user. For a newly created installation whose webhook has not been processed yet (or failed delivery), there is no sender metadata and no check, so an attacker who enumerates the sequential GitHub installation_id can link a victim's fresh installation to the attacker's Sentry org — exactly the attack this PR is meant to prevent. The check only protects re-linking of already-existing integrations.

adjudication.rationale: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the installer-verification (comparing pipeline state "github_authenticated_user" to integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]) is only executed after successfully fetching an existing ACTIVE Integration. On the `except Integration.DoesNotExist:` branch (when no Integration row exists for `external_id=installation_id`), the code immediately returns `pipeline.next_step()` without any check against `github_authenticated_user`. This is directly visible in the diff and means the new verification control is skipped entirely for the “Integration doesn’t exist yet” path, i.e., it only protects re-linking of already-existing integrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/test_gap] tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:385-455 (test_github_user_mismatch): This test never reaches the sender-mismatch branch it was written to exercise. Because installation_id is bound before the authorize redirect (changing pipeline.signature), the hardcoded state=9cae… cannot match the callback pipeline's signature, so the test fails at state validation and renders the generic error. The PR's central security comparison (github_authenticated_user vs integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]) is therefore never executed by any test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not support the claim that binding `installation_id` before redirect “changes `pipeline.signature`” such that the hardcoded `state=9cae…` cannot match. In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, `pipeline.bind_state("installation_id", …)` happens before `state = pipeline.signature` is sent to GitHub, and on the callback the pipeline is resumed from stored state; nothing in this diff indicates `pipeline.signature` mutates in a way that would force a mismatch. Also, `test_github_user_mismatch` performs the initial `init_path_2` request (which would establish pipeline state including `installation_id`) and then performs the callback request with `code`/`state`, which is consistent with reaching `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` and the sender/login comparison. While the test’s assertion is generic (it would pass for multiple failure paths), the finding’s definite explanation about state/signature mismatch is not verifiable from the PR diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:332-345 and :698-712: test_github_installed_on_another_org and test_github_prevent_install_until_pending_deletion_is_complete send the stale hardcoded state 9cae… after an init request that bound installation_id (which changes the signature). State validation fails and the response is "Invalid installation request.", so the asserted specific errors ("Github installed on another Sentry organization." / pending deletion) cannot be produced — these tests are broken as written. Capture the state from the authorize redirect's Location instead of hardcoding it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds strict state checking in `OAuthLoginView`: `if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature: return error(...)`. In `test_github_installed_on_another_org` and `test_github_prevent_install_until_pending_deletion_is_complete`, the callback requests use a hardcoded `state=9cae...` (`setup_path_2` / the second GET to `self.setup_path`) rather than extracting whatever state was actually issued in the preceding authorize redirect. These tests also perform multiple init/setup attempts within the same test (re-running `init_path_*`), which can create a new pipeline/signature; if the signature differs, the callback will hit the new “Invalid installation request.” branch and the asserted specific errors (another-org / pending-deletion) won’t be reachable. The finding’s core point—hardcoded state makes these tests incorrect/brittle under the new validation—is supported by the added state validation logic and the test code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:385-395 (test_installation_not_found): The test no longer exercises the installation-not-found path — the assertion was changed from "The GitHub installation could not be found." to "Invalid installation request." because the flow now terminates at the OAuth step (state/token exchange) before the 404 installation lookup ever runs. The 404 mock is dead weight, get_installation_info failure handling is now uncovered, and the test name is misleading.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `OAuthLoginView` before `GitHubInstallation` (`get_pipeline_views` now returns `[OAuthLoginView(), GitHubInstallation()]`). In `test_installation_not_found`, the flow was changed: it first GETs `setup_path` with only `installation_id` (which now hits `OAuthLoginView` and redirects to GitHub OAuth because there is no `state`), then GETs `setup_path` with `code` and a `state` that does not match the pipeline signature (`ddd0...` vs the expected signature used elsewhere like `9cae...`), which triggers the early `state` mismatch error path in `OAuthLoginView` (`return error(...)`). That means the test no longer reaches the installation lookup / `get_installation_info`-driven behavior, and the new assertion for "Invalid installation request." aligns with this earlier termination. The test name and coverage of the installation-not-found path are therefore misleading/uncovered based on this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:407-409 (OAuthLoginView.dispatch): redirect_uri (and the other params) are interpolated into the authorize URL via f-string without urlencode. Any reserved query character (&, =, space) in the absolute URI corrupts the query string / breaks the redirect. Build the query with urlencode.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the authorize URL is built via an f-string with `redirect_uri = absolute_uri(reverse(...))`. From the diff, `reverse("sentry-extension-setup", ...)` produces a fixed path (`/extensions/github/setup/` as asserted in tests), and `absolute_uri(...)` will add scheme/host. There’s no evidence in this diff that `redirect_uri` (or the other params) can contain `&`, `=`, or spaces that would corrupt the query string; the added tests even expect the unencoded URI to be used verbatim. While `urlencode` would be more robust in general, the finding claims a concrete breaking behavior that isn’t verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:113-115 and the error() default: The "We could not verify the authenticity of the installation request" message is also returned for transient failures (token exchange failure, user-info fetch failure, inactive integration), misattributing GitHub availability/config problems to authenticity and telling users to restart when restarting won't help. Distinguish these failure modes in the error message.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a generic `error()` helper whose default long message is `ERR_INTEGRATION_INVALID_INSTALLATION_REQUEST` (“We could not verify the authenticity…”). That default is used in multiple distinct failure cases that are not necessarily authenticity problems, e.g. OAuth token exchange / parsing issues or missing access token (`safe_urlopen` + `safe_urlread` + `parse_qsl`, then `if "access_token" not in payload: return error(...)`), user-info fetch/shape issues (`authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(...); if "login" not in ...: return error(...)`), and missing/ inactive Integration (`Integration.objects.get(..., status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` except -> `return error(...)`). This is misleading UX/documentation rather than a functional correctness defect, but it is specific and diff-grounded: distinguishing messages would improve user guidance.
